scenario.title: Thessaloniki - Evacuation
intro.text:
THESSALONIKI - EVACUATION - 9 APR 1941

Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia

Thessaloniki is not to hold - Evacuate your troops to Athens via sea immediately! The remains of the Krussia Detachment and the 19th Motorised Infantry Division try to kept clear your back as long as possible!

GOAL Retreat 9 ground units (in sea transport) via Exit Points or hold after the seventh turn 4 VH for BV! Hold after the seventh turn 3 VH or 2 VH for V or TV!

NOTE Due to the short time between the missions at HQ no new units can be recruited!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-5-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-5-0-briliant.text: The main columns reached the exits before German armour could split the road. Thessaloniki has received an army, though the harbour cannot promise room for all of it.
line.reaction-5-1-victory-tactical.text: Enough of the road remained open to keep the retreat moving. Some rear guards arrived at the port without their guns; some guns arrived without crews.
line.callback-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-0.text: The port officers have copied the closing-hour table from our road junctions. For once, an orderly retreat has convinced the next headquarters that order can be repeated.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: You pushed the combat columns through before the Thessaloniki road closed. The port received more veterans—and fewer men able to hold the approaches behind them.
line.callback-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-2.text: The Trebeshinë reserve is still a unit rather than a memory. It has been assigned every difficult slope since.
line.callback-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-3.text: The reserve was dissolved into the formation, leaving no famous battalion and fewer hollow companies.
line.scene-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-0.text: Nine berths, nine unit numbers. The hospital commandant has written names in every margin and sent the list back to me without a covering note.
line.scene-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-1.text: He thought the names were the note.
line.scene-2.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-2.text: The first tide can take formed battalions or stretchers. If it tries to take both, officers will settle the question at the gangway and the ships will sail half-loaded.
line.decision.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.decision.text: Who boards first: the units that can fight again, or the wounded and broken formations that cannot hold the quay?
line.decision.choice.embark-the-veterans: Give the first berths to formed combat units.
Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.
Load the hospital and broken units first; the veterans hold the quay.
Spend 75 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-0.text: The veterans get the first ship because they can survive waiting for the second. That is a soldier's joke, Commander, and I advise you not to repeat it on the quay.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-a-1.text: First tide to formed units. I will put the second sailing time in writing and hand it to the rear-guard commanders myself.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-b-0.text: The brigade commanders will say we embarked men who cannot be used while leaving behind men who can. They will be correct.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-1.text: And the hospital will move before dark. Tell the veterans the truth: they are buying those berths, and no ship is promised after the second tide.
